# Write a Polite but Firm Complaint Letter with ChatRTX

> **In short:** ChatRTX is a free AI chat app from NVIDIA that runs on your Windows PC, so your complaint stays private. Type what happened in your own words, and it rewrites it into a calm, firm letter you can send.

You've been put on hold for the third time, your refund is "still processing," and you just want someone to actually read what you're saying. Before you fire off an angry email you'll regret, open ChatRTX and let it turn your frustration into words that get results. This guide walks you through it, step by step.

## Before you start
- **A Windows PC with a recent NVIDIA RTX graphics card** (RTX 30, 40, or 50 series). ChatRTX runs the AI on your own computer instead of sending your letter to the cloud — that's a real privacy plus when you're describing a personal complaint.
- **ChatRTX installed.** If you haven't installed it yet, grab it free from NVIDIA's website and run the installer; it takes about 15 minutes the first time.
- **Your complaint notes.** A few bullet points in any app (Notepad is fine) about what went wrong, dates, names if you remember them, and what you'd like fixed (refund, replacement, apology).
- **Rough total time:** 10–15 minutes for your first letter, faster after that.

One honest note: ChatRTX only runs on NVIDIA RTX cards. If your PC has a different graphics card, this guide won't apply — most computers with at least 8 GB of VRAM and a modern NVIDIA GPU will handle it comfortably.

## Step 1 — Open ChatRTX and find the chat box
Double-click the **ChatRTX** icon on your desktop, or open the Start menu and type "ChatRTX." When the app is ready, you'll see a dark window with a long **text box at the bottom** and a send button (a paper airplane or arrow) on the right. The top of the window shows the model name (like "Llama" or "Mistral") — that's the AI you're about to talk to. If your window looks different, look for a **chat-style layout** with an empty input bar; some versions show a sidebar first, in which case click "New Chat" or the **+** icon to begin.
💬 Example: just leave the box empty for now — your first message is coming next.
You'll know it worked when the app finishes loading (a brief spinning icon stops) and the cursor blinks inside the chat box, ready for you to type.

## Step 2 — Paste in your messy notes
Click into the chat box and paste whatever you've written — even if it's rough. Bullet points, half-sentences, a rant, all fine. ChatRTX sees only what you paste; nothing else on your computer is touched. After you hit the send button, the AI takes a few seconds to a minute (depending on your PC) to read your notes. Because the AI runs locally on your graphics card, your complaint never leaves your computer — that's worth knowing if the situation is sensitive.
💬 Example: "Ordered a coffee maker March 2, arrived broken. Called support 3 times, told me to wait. Want a refund or a working replacement. Spent $129. This is the 3rd week."
You'll know it worked when the AI replies with a short acknowledgment or starts drafting the letter right away.

## Step 3 — Ask for a polite but firm letter
Now type a clear instruction telling the AI what you want. Be specific about the tone — "polite but firm" is the sweet spot: firm enough to be taken seriously, polite enough that a customer service rep will actually want to help you. Press Enter or click send. The AI will rewrite your notes into a proper letter with a greeting, the facts in order, and a clear ask at the end. If the first draft isn't quite right, just say so in a follow-up message — ChatRTX will try again with your feedback in mind.
💬 Example: "Turn this into a polite but firm complaint letter to the company. Include the date I ordered, what went wrong, how many times I called, and end with a clear ask: full refund within 7 days. Keep it under 200 words. Don't sound angry."
You'll know it worked when you see a finished letter with "Dear Customer Service," the facts laid out clearly, and a specific request at the end — not just a rephrased version of your rant.

## Step 4 — Add the small details that make it real
A complaint letter gets a real reply when it includes specifics the company can look up. Tell ChatRTX to weave in the order number, dates, and the names of anyone you spoke to (if you have them). The AI will fit them into the letter naturally. If you don't have an order number or names, skip this step — a polite letter without those details still beats no letter at all.
💬 Example: "Add my order number #CM-2026-04881, the dates March 2 and March 18, and that I spoke to a representative named 'Sara' on March 12. Don't invent anything else."
You'll know it worked when the finished letter includes those details in the right places — order number near the top, dates in the story, the rep's name where you mentioned the call.

## Step 5 — Read the letter out loud and tweak the tone
Copy the finished letter from ChatRTX (select the text, Ctrl+C, or look for a **copy icon** next to the message). Paste it into any document and read it out loud — yes, really. If you stumble over a sentence or it sounds harsher than you meant, paste it back into ChatRTX and ask for a softer or stronger version of just that paragraph. This is the step most people skip, and it's the one that gets you a real response instead of a form reply. Be honest with yourself: if it sounds rude to your own ears, it will sound rude to the person reading it.
💬 Example: "Soften the second paragraph only. I don't want to sound like I'm blaming anyone personally — just the situation."
You'll know it worked when you can read the whole letter without cringing, and you'd feel okay if a stranger read it back to you.

## Step 6 — Send the letter to the right place
Find the company's customer service email (usually on their website under "Contact us" or "Support"). Paste your letter into a new email, add a short subject line that summarizes the issue, attach any receipts or photos you have, and send. Keep a copy of the letter and the email thread in a folder — if you don't hear back in 5 business days, you'll send a polite follow-up, and ChatRTX can help you write that one too. Save the ChatRTX conversation so you can reuse the tone for any future letters.
💬 Example subject line: "Order #CM-2026-04881 — request for refund after 3 weeks of unresolved support"
You'll know it worked when the email lands in your "Sent" folder with the polished letter attached, ready to do its job.

## Common mistakes
- **Mistake: pasting a huge block of raw rage.** Fix it first: even three bullet points of facts give ChatRTX more to work with than a stream of anger. Calm input = calm output.
- **Mistake: trusting the first draft without reading it.** Fix: always read the letter out loud. The AI sometimes invents details or sounds stiffer than you intended — your eyes will catch it.
- **Mistake: forgetting to include the order number or dates.** Fix: if you have them, add them in Step 4. Companies can't help you if they can't find your account.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** the next time a delivery is late, a bill is wrong, or a service rep hangs up on you, you've already got a working process — type the facts, ask ChatRTX for a polite-but-firm letter, send it.
- **For your business or work:** the same workflow handles vendor disputes, late client payments, or a pushy salesperson. A calm, specific letter gets paid faster than a heated one.
- **If you're just getting started:** keep a "complaint notes" file on your desktop. The moment something annoys you, drop a line in there. By the time you're ready to write, your raw notes are already waiting.

## Try it now
Think of one small thing that's been bugging you this week — a wrong charge, a delayed order, a noisy neighbor. Open Notepad, jot three bullet points, then open ChatRTX and paste them in with this prompt: "Turn this into a polite but firm complaint letter, under 150 words." You'll have a draft in under two minutes.
